questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to be able to improve my spanish, and i liked the size of the city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not the easiest

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: An info meeting the first day. Other than that i asked the office, and other Erasmus students, which was a big help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Not the easiest, as I was searching for an apartment and not a room. Most places wont rent to you if you dont have a spanish NIE, salary, job contract, insurance etc. 
To rent a room in a shared flat is supposed to be way easier. 
At last I was lucky and found something really nice and cheap right before arrival.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I loved it. The city is really accesable with metro, busses and also walking and biking, and i thought most areas was nice and secure. I lived pretty "far" from centrum and the university, but I liked it a lot because I personally felt like I saw more of the city that way.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Again, no the easiest, But nothing that made the stay bad, just some confusion at the beginning, which i think is normal when you move to a new place. My advice would be to just ask other Erasmus students and the offices. Not all professors will be helpful in this area, as it is not their job

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: An info meeting, and some emails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up with some other clases than i thought i would, because a lot of the ones i wanted had the same time schedule or was not available in the spring semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask in the office if you are confused. Go to the info meeting. Go to the first classes to check if its something for you, most professors do an introduction to the class the first day.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very different from each course

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some courses very different. Some similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Español de America 
El español y las lenguas del mundo hispánico
Norma y uso correcto de español
Español coloquial
Español para extranjeros

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Español de America with David was an amazing course and amazing professor. 
Norma y uso correcto de español was also nice, if you are interested in reaching a more academic level of writing in spanish, in terms of correct use of signs and grammar. Español coloquial i also enjoyed and is very interesting, but the teaching is more conservative, without use of almost any visuals (powerpoint, blackboard etc.)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Valencia had an offer of free public transportation for people under 30 in the exact time period I was here, so I did not spend a single euro on that, unless I went out of the city, which was amazing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have not really used or heard a lot of any at the university. The city itself have a lot of possibilities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think they have a language exchange cafe once or twice, but i dont know what else.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Go out of the city to the suburbs or small citys nearby. Join facebook groups about the city, people often talk about a lot of ideas and tips in there that you can get inspired by. The city is very active and if you actively search for it, you can join and do a ton of things. 
Also the language class at centre de idiomas was a really helpfull and nice experience for me improving my spanish, but you can take classes in many languages, and they have an extremely cheap offer for erasmus students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
The Turia park, the waterfall in Buñol, the beaches, and the free museums. Go to areas in the city that you havent been, its almost always a nice suprise.  
Big other citys are also close like Madrid, Barcelona, Alicante etc., and you can sometimes find bus tickets for only 5 euros with ALSA

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: not really

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: not any specific

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: its more accepted to be a little late, its more normal to ask random people for help (like directions or whatever it might be) than in Copenhagen,

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be openminded 
Go to the classes at the university 
if you are learning spanish, speak it as much as you can, a little helps a lot

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: dont stress about the confusion in the beginning, it will all work out. ask locals about their favourite bars, restaurants, spots etc. use the parks.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the people, improving my spanish and the experience of studying in another university and country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: finding housing and getting registered in the courses

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: overall an amazing experience, a really good city and i learned a lot. im very grateful for the opportunity.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
